# A stronger equally informed exact ordinary route

The first small-model Gaussian rejection baseline beat CFTP. Before promoting a
practical advance, grant it the SAME harmonic projection that the coupling proof
uses. This produces a much stronger positive independent proposal, rather than
another CFTP parameter sweep.

Let P=B^T L_0^(-1)B and tau_e=P_ee. For fixed q and r, sample INDEPENDENT conductance
bits from the exactly known tilted priors

    ptilde_e/(1-ptilde_e) = [p_e/(1-p_e)] q^(-r tau_e/2).

Given X, put D_X=det(L_X)/det(L_0). Accept the proposal with probability

    a_X = q^((r/2) sum tau_e X_e) D_X^(-r/2).             (L1)

It lies in (0,1] by the same chord inequality used in REJECTION_BOUND. Multiplying
the product proposal density by (L1) cancels the tilt exactly, leaving a constant
times the desired conductance weight. On acceptance draw its conditional Gaussian
field with the SAME certified quantization engine. This is an ordinary positive
rejection sampler for the IDENTICAL normalized output, with no target-density,
normalizing-constant or mixing oracle. Rational determinants and computable scalar
powers are enough. No frame fitting or use of sampled CFTP outputs chooses the tilt.

The guarantee improves the Gaussian-proposal exponential rate. For lambda in[0,1],

    0 <= log(1+(q-1)lambda)-lambda logq <= d_q,
    d_q = log[(q-1)/logq]-1+logq/(q-1),                  (L2)

with continuous value d_1=0. There are k=n-1 nonzero eigenvalues, hence

    a_X >= exp[-r k d_q/2]  for EVERY proposal.           (L3)

At q=2, d_q is about .05966. This can make the exact ordinary route useful well
beyond the small example where untitled Gaussian rejection already wins. It still
has an exponential bound for fixed contrast and unbounded size; no all-size
polynomial guarantee follows from (L3). The CFTP theorem supplies that missing
worst-case guarantee. A fixed-attempt capped rejection followed by an independent
exact CFTP fallback remains exact, since every accepted proposal has the target law
and the independent fallback has the same law. This hybrid needs no estimate of
acceptance probability. Its actual total cost must include both algorithms.

These are standard determinant chords, leverage preconditioning and rejection
sampling ingredients. Historical priority of their combination here is UNKNOWN;
they must not be presented as an invented gene

# Total acquisition and computational cost

## 1. Input and operation

The input is a supplied finite connected graph, rational q>=1, rational priors in
(0,1), integer component count r>=1, and rational output grid width delta>0.
More generally a supplied rational spanning frame and fixed PSD grounding matrix
are admitted by the theorem, although the executable specializes to a graph.
The baseline precision must be SPD. No unknown material potential is reconstructed.
There is no preparation, readout, bath or instrument oracle: this is computation
of the supplied model. It does not use N675 or any other unqualified Astra premise.

Choose a warranted rational c_bar<1 with

    r q(sqrt(q)-1)^2/8 <= c_bar.

The executable checks this inequality by a rational square comparison when the
sharpened bound is supplied. At q=1 the independent Gaussian/bit shortcut is an
ordinary faster option. Let k=n-1 be the pinned dimension.

## 2. Conditional update and arithmetic cost

After initial exact inversion, each state update uses O(k^2) rational arithmetic
for a matrix-vector contraction and Sherman--Morrison correction. The generic
implementation stores dense matrices. It does NOT turn an O(k) mesh into O(log k)
cost, use a free effective-resistance oracle, or claim optimal sparse complexity.
Graph/frame construction and inversion are charged separately in the receipt.

On a unit graph with rational q of bit length B, every possible precision has
integer-scaled entries of bit length O(B+log m). Cofactors and the determinant
bound every reduced inverse entry's bit length by O(k(B+log m+log k)). This bound
depends on the input size, not the history of rank updates. Rational Gaussian
elimination and LDL also have polynomial bit bounds via determinant minors.
For a general rational frame, replace B by its full entry bit-height; clearing
denominators and the same determinant argument still apply.

The expected state-update count is <=8L, with

    L=ceil[m(ceil(log2 m)+1)/(1-c_bar)].

The proof also gives all fixed moments of the largest window/replayed update
count bounded polynomially in L. The explicit dependence on 1/(1-c_bar) is REAL;
being extremely close to the contrast boundary is not computationally free.

# Result: exact centered harmonic-mixture equilibrium output

Completed private proof/implementation/controls. Independent whole review is pending.

The attempted capability was local thermal computation in a gapless anharmonic
medium without global equilibration. The result changes that question to a paid
FINITE global operation: normalized independent quantized full-field output for a
supplied centered, bounded-contrast Gaussian-mixture model, including nonconvex
edge potentials. No material potential, infinite background or mixing oracle is
granted. The intended infinite-volume local-cost capability is NOT_ACHIEVED.

For any finite connected graph, r components, conductance ratio q, and arbitrary
edge priors in(0,1), the new common-configuration current sum gives the sufficient
contraction

    c = r q(sqrt(q)-1)^2/8 <1.

It needs neither graph dimension/degree nor a lower bound on the height spectral
gap. Monotone CFTP then takes O(m log m)/(1-c) expected exact conditional queries.
The code pays dense rational inverse updates, not a free local resistance oracle.
The same theorem holds for a supplied rational spanning frame with PSD grounding.
The implementation specializes to graph incidences and constant prior.

After stiffness sampling, rational LDL plus persistent fair-bit Box--Muller/Arb
intervals return the WHOLE requested finite-grid field, with no float-governed
branch, cutoff or ambiguous-output replacement. Constructive scalar arithmetic
pays a finite mean bit-work theorem. The seeded executions are diagnostics;
installed-library expected CPU bit complexity is not certified.

The declared23.98-second batch includes full outputs up to63 coordinates,
nonconvex q4,p99/100 and three-component cases. Exact determinant/current/inverse
controls and a forced CFTP replay passed. The single Monte Carlo cycle statistic
was -0.3513 standard errors and is retained as diagnostic only. No physical action
occurred and no statistical result is a proof of the universal theorem.

leverage-tilted independent determinant rejection, supplied the SAME harmonic

beats dense CFTP by about28.8x on64 outputs of the16-site model and129.7x on2
